subject: modeling correlation of binary and real outcomes

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: modeling correlation of binary and real outcomes
parts:
Hi stan-users,

I've got one binary outcome and several real outcomes per observation
and I'd like to model the correlation among the outcomes using a normal
model. Right now I'm just trying to recover the correlation parameters
from simulated data.

The binary outcome is hooked into the model with a latent variable.

Is there a better way to write this model? Is there a way to avoid
creating the temporary variable `z1`?

data {
int<lower=0> N; // observations
int<lower=0> P; // input variables (first is binary)
int<lower=0, upper=1> x1[N]; // binary data
vector[P-1] x[N]; // real valued data
}
parameters {
vector[P] mu;
corr_matrix[P] Omega; // corr
vector<lower=0>[P] tau; // scale
real z1[N]; // latent variable for the binary data
}
transformed parameters {
vector[P] z[N];
for (n in 1:N)
z[n][1] <- z1[n];

for (n in 1:N)
for (p in 2:P)
z[n][p] <- x[n][p - 1];
}
model {
tau ~ normal(0, 1);
Omega ~ lkj_corr(P);
mu ~ normal(0, 1);

z ~ multi_normal(mu, quad_form_diag(Omega, tau));
for (n in 1:N)
x1[n] ~ bernoulli_logit(z[n][1]);
}

Thanks,

Allen

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling correlation of binary and real outcomes
parts:
Not sure why you took the LKJ prior parameter
to be the number of inputs.

And you want to use the Cholesky-factor parameterization.

But I wouldn't worry about the temp (though I'd make it a temp
in the model block rather than a saved transformed parameter);
the loops and assignments are pretty much free compared to the
real work of computing derivatives.

- Bob

append_col (or maybe it's append_column). If you're looking for the other direction, append_row.

There should be accessors for that. Check the same section in the manual. All the slicing functions are in the same section.
